title: Yose ben Choni
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A Tanna mentioned in Mishnah Zevachim 1:2: he rules that sacrifices slaughtered with the designation of a Passover offering or a sin offering are invalid. Shimon, brother of Azaryah, disagrees.
Pesachim 73b has Yosef ben Chonai. Hyman suggests he may be the sage in Nazir 23a, where a baraita is recited in the name of Rabbi Yose bar Rav (Rabbi) Choni: why is the vav of uvekumah dotted?

notes.text: The parenthetical Rabbi after Rav in the Choni name and the attribution boundary remain unclear. Hyman’s possible identification with the other Yose/Yosef forms is not adopted as fact.

The saved whole Davidson Nazir 23a scalar explicitly introduces a baraita in Rabbi Yose bar Rav Choni's name and asks why the elder daughter's uvekumah has a dotted vav. This resolves the earlier attribution-boundary objection for that named passage, without deleting Hyman's parenthetical (Rabbi) after Rav. An alternative father's title is plausible, not demonstrated editorial history. Yose/Yosef, ben/bar and Choni/Chonai remain distinct forms, and Hyman's POSSIBLE identification with the Zevachim figure remains conjectural. Other cited passages were not newly inspected; the entry's hold classification is retained pending a separate clearance gate.

Pesachim 73b cites the ruling of Mishnah Zevachim 1:2 under the name Yosef ben Chonai. Nazir 23a introduces the question about the dotted vav in the elder daughter’s uvekumah in the name of Rabbi Yose bar Rav Choni, without Hyman’s parenthetical “Rabbi.” The proposed connection with the Nazir figure is Hyman’s.
